test_title: Most Repeated 2025 General Science PYQ Subject Test - 01
subject: gk
question: What property distinguishes a compound from a mixture?

options.text: There is a fixed balance and characteristics

solution:
The correct answer is __**There is a fixed balance and characteristics**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **compound** is a substance formed when two or more chemical elements are **chemically bonded** together. The most defining characteristic of a compound is that the elements are always present in **fixed ratios** by mass.
 
• This fixed ratio is governed by the **Law of Definite Proportions** (also known as **Proust's Law**), which states that a chemical compound always contains its component elements in a fixed ratio and does not depend on its source or method of preparation.
 
• Unlike mixtures, the formation of a compound involves a **chemical change**, resulting in a product with **entirely different properties** from its constituent elements. For example, **Sodium** (a reactive metal) and **Chlorine** (a toxic gas) combine to form **Sodium Chloride** (common table salt).
 
• Compounds possess a **fixed melting and boiling point**, which serves as a benchmark for their **purity**. Because they are held together by chemical bonds (ionic or covalent), they cannot be separated by simple **physical methods** like filtration or evaporation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mixtures**:

 
 
• Components are physically combined and can be present in **any proportion**.
 
• They retain the **original properties** of their constituents (e.g., in a mixture of iron and sulfur, iron remains magnetic).
 
• They can be **homogeneous** (uniform composition like **Alloys**) or **heterogeneous** (non-uniform like **Soil**).
 
• Separation is possible through **physical processes** such as **distillation**, **sublimation**, or **magnetism**.
 
 
 
• **Separation of Compounds**:
 
 
• Compounds can only be broken down into their individual elements through **chemical reactions** or **electrochemical reactions** like **electrolysis**.
 
 
 
• **States of Matter**:
 
 
• The option **Always solid** is incorrect because compounds can exist in all three states of matter: **solid** (Calcium Carbonate), **liquid** (Water), and **gas** (Carbon Dioxide).
